Use FEniCS legacy (dolfin) for a 2D small-strain linear elasticity solve.
The domain is an L-shape: the unit square [0,1]×[0,1] with the top-right sub-square [0.5,1]×[0.5,1] removed as a notch.
Mesh with 64 elements per edge of the outer 1×1 square, with the notch carved out consistently; use unit thickness.
Material is linear isotropic plane stress with E = 70e9 Pa, ν = 0.33, using the reduced plane-stress constitutive law (effective λ = E·ν/(1−ν²), μ = E/(2(1+ν))).
Density is ρ = 2700 kg/m³.
Solve on a vector-valued displacement function space (degree 2 Lagrange elements recommended) with a direct linear solver.
Constrain the left boundary x = 0 fully clamped (u = (0,0)).
Apply a body force b = (0, −ρ·g) = (0, −26487) N/m³ over the entire L-shaped domain (gravity downward in −y).
Apply a normal traction σ_yy = −2.65e4·y Pa (compressive, varying linearly with the global y-coordinate) on the outer right edge x = 1, which with the top-right notch spans y ∈ [0, 0.5] (traction 0 at y = 0 rising to −1.325e4 Pa at y = 0.5).
Do not apply any traction based on the x-coordinate; all other boundaries, including the re-entrant inner notch boundaries (y = 0.5, x ∈ [0.5,1] and x = 0.5, y ∈ [0.5,1]), are traction-free.
After solving, compute the in-plane Cauchy stress field (σ_xx, σ_yy, σ_xy) and evaluate the von Mises stress from the in-plane components.
Output the displacement field and stress/von Mises distributions over the L-shaped domain.
